page: Microsoft Azure D48alds_v6 is a compute-oriented virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz. Utilizing the x86_64 architecture under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance provides 48 dedicated vCPUs distributed across 24 physical cores with two threads per core. System memory is configured at 96.0 GB, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The hardware incorporates instruction set extensions including AVX-512, VNNI, and BF16, alongside hardware cryptographic engines like VAES and SHA-NI.

The instance includes 2835 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage for high-throughput ephemeral scratch capacity, in addition to supporting Azure Premium Storage. The configuration does not include discrete GPU hardware accelerators. Memory caching features 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache pool.

Synthetic benchmarks demonstrate upper-quartile processing capabilities, with top 25% results in single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests, PassMark CPU tests, and Geekbench suites. Parallel compute throughput is verified by elevated scores in Clang software compilation and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Cached small-block memory reads achieve high transfer rates, supporting high transaction volumes such as over 66 million Redis operations per second. However, uncached 256 MB memory transfers register in the average middle tier, and large-parameter language model generation is constrained by available memory capacity and the absence of GPU acceleration.

Given its high core count relative to memory and large bundled NVMe storage, Microsoft Azure D48alds_v6 offers strong qualitative cost efficiency for CPU-intensive parallel tasks needing fast local scratch space. It is appropriate for CI/CD build pipelines, distributed batch compute, microservices hosting, and localized database workloads with working sets that align with its 96 GB RAM capacity.
